answers.question: What are we building?
answers.answer: A certificate issuer and public record where each credential is signed by its office, bound to a verified identity and verifiable from the anchored record.
answers.why: A certificate that any office can forge is worth nothing, so the model binds each one to a signature and an identity.

answers.question: Who uses it?
answers.answer: Issuing officers sign. Holders present. Employers, banks and other offices verify through the record.
answers.why: The verifier reads the anchored record alone and needs no call to the issuing office.

answers.question: What has to be true on day one?
answers.answer: Every certificate carries an electronic signature from a named office and an identity binding verified through the citizen identity module.
answers.why: Those two rules make the record provable without the paper.

answers.question: How does the system reach the outside world?
answers.answer: The system reaches no outside network. The package installs from media and carries every dependency with it.
answers.why: A Government deployment runs inside an air gapped site, so every part travels in the package rather than over a connection.

answers.question: Where does the data live?
answers.answer: Storage and processing stay inside the declared national jurisdiction.
answers.why: The residency lock is enforced at the infrastructure layer and the manifest records it, so a reviewer reads the position rather than asking for it.

answers.question: Who agrees to a change?
answers.answer: A structural change needs agreement from Issuing Office, Registrar, Audit Authority.
answers.why: Governance across organisations is standard for Government, so one department changes the shared record with the others agreeing.

answers.question: How long do we keep the records?
answers.answer: Every collection keeps its records for 30 years unless the template states a longer span.

retention.statement: Every procurement collection keeps its records for ten years, which covers the audit period and any later challenge. The template states every retention span in whole years.

extended.statement: A tender stays readable for ten years so a challenge reaches the published notice.
A sealed bid stays readable for ten years so an auditor compares the offers behind an award.
An order stays readable for ten years so the three way match survives an inspection.

organisations.title: Procurement Department
organisations.summary: The department that publishes a tender and awards it.

organisations.title: Audit Authority
organisations.summary: The authority that inspects award decisions after the fact.

organisations.title: Finance Ministry
organisations.summary: The ministry that releases the budget behind an award.

governance.statement: Every structural change requires agreement across the named organisations. One organisation changes the shared record with the others agreeing.

quorum.summary: A routine change passes on a simple majority inside the owning organisation.
A change that moves public money passes with two organisations agreeing.
A structural change passes with three organisations agreeing and waits two days before it takes effect.
A change to the governance itself passes with three organisations agreeing and waits seven days.

stages.summary: The owning department writes the change and states the reason a person reads.
Every named organisation reads the change and records a position.
The organisations record agreement and the waiting period starts.
The change takes effect and the manifest records the new position.

answers.question: What are we building?
answers.answer: An open procurement record that carries a tender from the published notice to the goods receipt.
answers.why: Every step rests on one record, so a supplier and a citizen read the same account of an award.

answers.question: Who uses it?
answers.answer: Procurement officers publish and award. Suppliers bid. Receiving clerks record goods. Auditors inspect.
answers.why: The permission matrix narrows each role to the fields and the rows its work needs.

answers.question: What has to be true on day one?
answers.answer: A bid stays sealed until the close, and an award carries a written ground.
answers.why: Those two rules carry the fairness the process promises, so the Blueprint holds them as invariants rather than as guidance.

answers.question: How does the system reach the outside world?
answers.answer: The system reaches no outside network. The package installs from media and carries every dependency with it.
answers.why: A Government deployment runs inside an air gapped site, so every part travels in the package rather than over a connection.

answers.question: Where does the data live?
answers.answer: Storage and processing stay inside the declared national jurisdiction.
answers.why: The residency lock is enforced at the infrastructure layer and the manifest records it, so a reviewer reads the position rather than asking for it.

answers.question: Who agrees to a change?
answers.answer: A structural change needs agreement from Procurement Department, Audit Authority, Finance Ministry.
answers.why: Governance across organisations is standard for Government, so one department changes the shared record with the others agreeing.

answers.question: How long do we keep the records?
answers.answer: Every collection keeps its records for 10 years unless the template states a longer span.
answers.why: Government retention defaults run longer than the commercial defaults, and the manifest states each span in plain words.

answers.question: What are we building?
answers.answer: A public vote that publishes its roll size, its sealed votes and every station total.
answers.why: A result anybody recomputes needs no trust in the body that declared it.

answers.question: Who uses it?
answers.answer: Returning officers open and declare. Presiding officers seal votes and publish totals. Observers recompute. Voters check a receipt.
answers.why: The observer is a role in the model with a credential, so a recount is an ordinary read.

answers.question: What has to be true on day one?
answers.answer: Votes recorded never exceed the roll, and every voter holds a receipt.
answers.why: Those two rules carry the two questions a contested result always asks.
